AbstractText.Label: Purpose:
AbstractText.content: To evaluate postoperative pain in patients submitted to conventional laparoscopic cholecystectomy with four ports versus single-port laparoscopic cholecystectomy with only one port.

AbstractText.Label: Methods:
AbstractText.content: Twenty-one patients were included in the conventional laparoscopic cholecystectomy group and 19 other patients in the single-port laparoscopic cholecystectomy group. A VAS was used for the assessment of postoperative pain at three time points. Differences were considered statistically significant when p<0.05.

AbstractText.Label: Results:
AbstractText.content: Intergroup analysis showed no significant difference in VAS scores between the conventional laparoscopic cholecystectomy and single-port laparoscopic cholecystectomy groups at any of the time points studied.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusion:
AbstractText.content: This study found no significant difference in postoperative pain between the two groups.
